3.measure_note: legacy_colAB Schedule A underline form. rowbands.py (200 dpi, raw frame, skew +0.0) returns 17 per-column underline rules from 18.89 at a regular pitch of 4.07, each carrying the 4 segments that ARE the column bands (Date 6.47-18.25, Name 19.84-53.68, Address 55.27-83.23, Amount 84.81-95.06). THE TEXT SITS ABOVE ITS UNDERLINE, so row N spans [rule N-1, rule N] and row 1 is extrapolated one pitch up from the first rule (18.89 - 4.07 = 14.82). This page has exactly ONE transcribed row, so it is proved directly: the 900 dpi crop pct:84.81,14.82,10.25,4.07@p3 rendered '500.00' (recorded 500.00), sitting on its underline with the blank row below it empty.

4.measure_note: Same underline grid as p3 (skew -0.1): 17 rules from 19.41 at pitch 4.05; column bands Date 6.46-18.24, Name 19.83-53.67, Address 55.20-83.22, Amount 84.80-95.05. Row 1 extrapolated one pitch up (19.41 - 4.05 = 15.36); rows 2-5 are [rule N-1, rule N]. TWO-CROP PROOF at 900 dpi: the FIRST transcribed row's amount box pct:84.80,15.36,10.25,4.05@p4 rendered '21.52' (recorded 21.52) and the LAST transcribed row's amount box pct:84.80,31.61,10.25,4.05@p4 rendered '128.00' (recorded 128.00) — the ends of the ledger, so the five bands are not shifted. A 700 dpi control crop of the Name column across rows 2-4 (pct:19.83,19.41,33.84,12.20@p4) rendered 'Carol's Copies' / 'Monogram Station' / 'Carol's Copies' in that order, confirming the middle bands line up with the names as well as the amounts.
